Additionally, a standard upper gastrointestinal contrast series utilizing barium may be required for assessment of anatomy of the
gastrointestinal tract (Fig. 1). Children with food allergies, repetitive vomiting, or abdominal pain may also need endoscopic eval-
uation, and some children will also need colonoscopy to rule out the possibility of underlying inﬂammatory disease such as eosin-
ophilic gastroenteropathy. Gastroenterology consultation can help determine the utility of these studies. Depending on
symptomatology and physical exam, some children may need cranial imaging to look for evidence of intracranial mass lesions,
hydrocephaly, or posterior fossa anomalies, such as the Chiari malformation. If allergic disease is suspected, consultation with
a pediatric allergist is recommended.
